zones.label: Column 1
zones.note: Lexical aid: Entry Words Data of Nippojisho, NINJAL, Hideyuki Ohshima and Taichi Aida, version 202510, CC BY 4.0. Consulted after independent scan reading; its readings do not determine this copy's typography. https://www2.ninjal.ac.jp/textdb_dataset/en/nipp/index.html ; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

lines.note: Sakiyaburi describes tearing something apart. The scan gives initial S and the doubled t in utta, not OCR Baqiyaburi or uta; the explanation continues on the following row.
Completes the preceding definition with breaking or tearing into pieces. This is an indented body continuation, not a separate entry.
Sara is a dish, here explained as a basin or a small sauce dish. The second Portuguese noun has two long-s forms, not f.

runs.text: Ficai em bora, ou ide embora. ¶ Itẽ,

lines.note: Saraba supplies a leave-taking expression addressed either to the person staying or to the person departing. The source varies em bora and embora on this same row; the abbreviated Itẽ introduces another use.
Continues saraba with an encouraging exclamation and the connective sense 'since that is so.' Eyaſus and the unseparated Iaque are Portuguese, not Japanese examples.

The gloss means 'if even so, how much more ...' and P. marks poetic usage. The tall third consonant supports printed Sadedani, also found in the supplied NINJAL index; its editorial suggestion Saradedani is not adopted into the transcription. Quãto, not OCR quãtao, is visible.

runs.text: Hum inſtrumento de bambu como pen-

lines.note: Sarai names a bamboo rake, compared with a comb. The printed pen- is explicitly divided before tem on the next row.

runs.text: tem comque ajuntam folhas das aruores caidas,

lines.note: Completes the comb comparison and explains gathering fallen tree leaves. Comque remains joined as printed, and the row is indented beneath the headword.
Finishes the rake's uses with collecting litter or other material. Ciſco is Portuguese debris, not an additional Japanese word.

runs.text: Couſa de pouco fundo, como bacio, ou

lines.note: This separate sarai entry means shallow, illustrated by a basin or tray. It must not be merged with the preceding tool-name homograph.
Bandeja completes the shallow-vessel comparison. The upright X. is the dictionary's regional usage label, outside the italic Portuguese gloss.
Sarameki denotes being rough or coarse. The principal forms qu and eita belong to the Japanese verb; the tight printed couſaaſpera is retained rather than editorially respaced.
Completes the roughness definition with 'coarse like stone.' The indentation and Portuguese type connect it to sarameqi.

runs.text: Aduerb. De nenhũa maneira com verbos

lines.note: Sarani is labelled an adverb; with negative verbs its sense is 'in no way.' The grammatical qualification continues on the following row.

runs.text: negatiuos. ¶ Itẽ, Denouo, ou doutra maneira.

lines.note: Closes the negative construction, then gives 'anew' or 'in another way' as further senses. The source's Denouo is not modernized or separated.

The example says that this will be done afresh or differently. The scan supports capital Coreuo and Portuguese iſto, not OCR asto; xôzu retains its visible circumflex. The printed ou- continues below.
Completes outro modo nouo: doing it in another, new way. This row belongs to the preceding example rather than beginning a new sense.
Saranu tei is a pretence or an appearance of unconcern, matching dissimulation. The initial is S, correcting OCR Baranu.
The repeated adverb describes doing something lightly and smoothly. Fazer has f, not OCR long s; no hyphen is visible after the divided al at the right rule.

runs.text: gũa couſa ligeira, & expeditamente, ou ler algũa

lines.note: Continues alguma and adds the application to reading fluently. The first and last tildes belong to u; the intervening Portuguese describes quick, unimpeded action.

runs.text: couſa ſem empeçar, nem gaguejar, &c. Item,

lines.note: Reading is done without stumbling or stammering. Enlargement supports gaguejar with a after j, replacing OCR gaguejer; Item begins another application.

runs.text: Modo de correr de cima agoa, ſangue, &c.

lines.note: Gives flowing down or off a surface, exemplified by water and blood. De cima qualifies the flow and is not a Japanese phrase.
Sararito is the shorter adverbial form, referred back to the senses immediately above. Idem does not introduce missing text.
The spaced reduplication sara sara shares those senses; a further construction starts with Com and continues below. The worn grammatical label is read as Aduerb., not the OCR fragment Adu rb.
With a negative, sara sara means 'not at all.' The first letter of nenhũa is n, not OCR m, and the whole line continues the preceding grammatical condition.
Sara sarato describes a rubbing or rustling motion. The initial is capital S, not OCR ç; the Portuguese construction continues with ir contas on the next row.

runs.text: ir contas entre as mãos, l, de ir correndo, &c.

lines.note: Explains passing or rubbing beads between the hands, then gives moving along at a run as an alternative. The printed wording eſfregar a / ir is retained; l is the alternative marker, not the numeral one.
Begins the example about two people crossing over a bridge briskly. Faxino vyeuo supplies 'over the bridge'; the Japanese sentence has not ended at this physical row.

Hashiriwatari completes the running-across example. No separate initial o is supported before f; that OCR addition is removed. The Portuguese says that both were running and prints a hyphen after corrẽ.

runs.text: do por cima da ponte ſemparar nem tropeçar.

lines.note: Completes the example: over the bridge without stopping or stumbling. The scan supports final tropeçar, not tropeçor, while the source's joined ſemparar remains unchanged.
Sarashi is the verb for bleaching or preparing cloth. The Portuguese specifies linen and begins the divided fabric name can-gas; the principal forms retain the historical aita ending.

Completes cangas and then introduces a transferred sense with Permet. Haji wo sarasu means exposing one's shame. The OCR's isolated Japanese-looking que was spurious: gas, &c. and Permet. are italic Portuguese apparatus.

The first gloss means becoming ashamed. Kabane wo sarasu then describes exposing or leaving one's corpse; the worn e in Cabaneuo is preferred to OCR c on the surviving strokes and the corpse gloss, but remains a nonblocking damaged-glyph reading.

runs.text: xar a vida no campo, ou o corpo ſem ſepultura.

lines.note: Completes deixar: leaving one's life on the battlefield, or one's body unburied. This is the explanation of the corpse example, not a separate entry.
Toga wo sarasu is to disclose one's faults or sins. Manifeſtar requires the visible f after i; the OCR's Maniſestar confused letter identities rather than merely s-allographs.

Gakumon ni manako wo sarasu refers to applying one's eyes to study. The second n is worn but belongs to the particle ni after gacumon; OCR ui would misread that construction. The Portuguese Dar- continues below.

runs.text: ſe muito ao estudo, ou estar ſempre ſobre o liuro.

lines.note: Finishes dar-se: devoting oneself to study or always poring over a book. The provisional st expansions in estudo and estar are retained for the project's dedicated ligature audit.

This nominal sarashi entry refers contextually to prepared or bleached cloth. Enlargement nevertheless shows the anomalous printed nonos, not a securely legible panos; nonos is preserved rather than silently correcting the source.
Saraye denotes cleaning out, illustrated by a water conduit. The Portuguese noun is cano, with a damaged final o rather than OCR c; dagoa retains the historical contraction.
Adds a spring to the cleaning examples, then gives inomoto wo sarayuru. Its meaning is established by the following explicit Portuguese gloss 'clean the well.'
The first clause means cleaning the well. Hori wo sarayuru then concerns cleaning a ditch or moat; the scan's worn ri supports Foriuo rather than OCR Fonuo.
Completes the ditch example with 'clean the ditch.' Alimpar is one word; the OCR's internal space has no basis in the printed type.
Sareba is explained as 'thus, that being so.' Aduerb. is a single italic grammatical label, not OCR A duerb.
Sareba koso strengthens the causal connection: 'precisely for that reason.' The headword is printed continuously despite the worn b; the OCR split Sareb acoſo is removed.
Saredomo is the adversative 'however' or 'nevertheless.' The scan has no i between d and o, correcting Sarediomo; no terminal punctuation is supplied beyond the visible &c.
Sarei is the etiquette of tea, explained by cha no rei and Portuguese courtesies or formal greeting. The scan reads Sarei and Corteſias, not the OCR's Saiei and Corteſſas.

runs.text: que ſe fazem antes. de beber o Cha.

lines.note: Specifies courtesies performed before drinking tea. The small mark after antes is a visible full stop; the unusual punctuation is retained rather than regularizing the sentence. Cha remains in the printed italic gloss.
Sari is to depart or separate oneself. Toco- begins tokoro wo saru across the column boundary; it is body text, not a catchword, and the printed hyphen is preserved.

runs.text: Irſe, ou apartarſe de algũ lugar.

lines.note: Completes Toco- from the preceding column as tokoro wo saru: to leave or withdraw from a place. This is a normal body continuation, with the example divided across the columns.

Sarigenai is described as dissimulation or pretence. The damaged n in the headword is supported by the remaining type and the following adverbial forms; the gloss begins dißimulação, not OCR ciſimulação.
Completes fingi-mento, 'pretence.' This short physical continuation must remain a body line with its own crop.
Gives the adverbial forms sarigenau and sarigenaku. The visible caron is retained on ǒ; the derived input kana is not used to change that historical form. The label and following gloss are italic.
Explains acting or speaking in a feigned manner. Falar has f rather than OCR long s, as both the letter and the coordinated Portuguese verbs show.
Sarinagara is an adversative connective, 'but' or 'nevertheless.' The short definition is complete on this row.
Saritomo is first glossed as complete assurance or absence of doubt. Item opens another use which occupies the next several lines.

runs.text: Palaura com que hum moſtra ter confiança,

lines.note: Describes an expression by which a person shows confidence. The sentence continues with having a good opinion of someone, rather than ending at the comma.
Finishes the confidence definition and introduces a Japanese verse example. Vt. is part of the italic explanatory apparatus.
The verse says that another's trusting expectation is precisely what causes sadness. The circumflex on vomôran is visible, and the line ends in a comma, omitted by the OCR.

Continues the verse about not knowing the speaker's precarious condition. The worn opening is read Arunimo, not OCR Aiunimo; the r is damaged. The parallel wording in Ise monogatari, section 65, supports aru ni mo aranu without establishing this copy's typography (parallel transcription: https://0p2nirt8qpfr.blog.fc2.com/blog-date-201102.html). This remains a nonblocking damaged-letter choice.

runs.text: O ter bõ cõceito de mim, ou cuidar bem de meu

lines.note: Begins the Portuguese rendering: having a good opinion of me or thinking well of my condition. The abbreviation tildes in bõ and cõceito remain unexpanded.

runs.text: eſtado iſto he o que me entriſtece, não ſabẽdo

lines.note: Continues that this confidence is what saddens the speaker, while the other person does not know the facts. The worn text supports iſto and entriſtece rather than the OCR fragments; the visible abbreviation over e is retained in ſabẽdo.

runs.text: parte de mim, nem de como eſtou.

lines.note: Finishes the translation with ignorance of the speaker and of how the speaker is situated. It completes the preceding Portuguese sentence, not a new Japanese entry.
Gives saritomo to koso with the same force as the preceding example. The source and supplied lexical index support tomoto, correcting OCR tomaio.

runs.text: Palaura de ſe eſpantar, ou enca-

lines.note: Saritote wa is an expression of astonishment or strong emphasis. The headword is unseparated in the print; enca- begins encarecer below.
Completes the sense of emphasizing something, then starts an example. The Japanese adjective is visibly divided vôqi-na, with a circumflex over o and a terminal hyphen.

runs.text: Por certo que he hũa grande

lines.note: Completes 'a great injustice or unreasonable act.' Murigia represents the Japanese predicative phrase; the following italic Portuguese begins its emphatic translation.
Completes grande sem razão, a great injustice or unreasonable action. The apparent shortness does not make this a catchword or marginal note.

runs.text: Bugio. ¶ Item, Hum dos animais por

lines.note: Saru is a monkey. A second sense introduces the animal's use in the cyclical reckoning described on the following rows.

runs.text: onde os Iapoes como por ſignos celeſtes contão

lines.note: Explains that the Japanese count using animal signs. Iapoes is the Portuguese people-name; the worn e was misread as c by OCR. The gloss itself compares these with celestial signs, without requiring a modern astronomical interpretation.

runs.text: os annos, ou as horas. Vt,

lines.note: Specifies years and hours, then gives saru no toki, the monkey hour, as an example. The Japanese example remains upright after italic Vt.

runs.text: As 4. horas da tarde, pouco mais, ou menos.

lines.note: The dictionary equates the monkey hour approximately with four in the afternoon. The printed stop after 4 is retained; the OCR's stray e and mats are removed in favor of horas and mais.

runs.text: Por quanto aßi he, ou ſendo aßi.

lines.note: Saru aida is a connective meaning 'because that is so' or 'that being so.' The headword begins Saru, not OCR Siru; the two Portuguese occurrences of aßi are retained in their printed form.
Sarude describes restless or fidgeting hands. The Japanese r-u sequence was misread as ni in Sanide; the Portuguese adjectives agree with mãos, including final inquietas.

runs.text: Os que fazem voltear, ou bailar os

lines.note: Saruhiki names people who make monkeys perform tricks or dance. Fazem begins with f, correcting the OCR long s.
Completes the object of the preceding verbs: monkeys. The short row remains part of the sarufiqi definition.
Gives saru hoko ni with the explanatory saru hodo ni, 'that being so.' The scan supports Sarufoconi and fodoni rather than OCR Surufoconi and fadoni; the forms are not modernized.

runs.text: paßãdo as couſas deſta maneira. ¶ Item, He

lines.note: Continues 'things proceeding in this manner,' then introduces another discourse use. The abbreviation tilde in paßãdo is preserved.

runs.text: palaura com que ſe começa algum liuro modeſ-

lines.note: Explains that the expression can begin a book modestly. The printed division modeſ-tamente belongs to the physical lineation.

runs.text: tamente dando a entender que não he aquillo no-

lines.note: Completes modestamente and explains the implied modesty: the material is not claimed as new. The source prints no- before uo below.

runs.text: uo, nem o que começa a dizer primeiro, co-

lines.note: Continues the denial of novelty or of being the first to speak of the matter. Co- introduces como across the next row break.
Completes como and compares the introductory expression somo somo. The scan has Somoſomo, without OCR's extra n; here it is a Japanese term embedded in Portuguese explanation.

runs.text: Peßoas que fazem autos, ou farſas:

lines.note: Sarugaku is explained here through its performers, who present plays or farces. Farſas begins with f, not OCR long s, and a colon is visible at the right edge.

runs.text: entre os quaes a cabeça, & principal ſe chama

lines.note: Introduces the title of the head or chief performer. The Portuguese sentence continues directly with Tayǔ on the next row.
Tayǔ is the title named by the preceding Portuguese sentence; its accent is a caron, not OCR's tilde. The upright Japanese example means performing sarugaku, and Fa- starts its translation.
Completes fazer autos: to perform plays. This is the translated example, not an independent entry.
The dictionary explicitly prefers sarigenai to sarugenai and directs the reader above. Meliùs and Vide are italic editorial apparatus; Sariguenai corrects OCR's missing r.
Completes Vide suprà, the backward reference. The grave accent belongs to the printed Latin direction.

runs.text: Certa laya de melões, no Cami.

lines.note: Defines this headword as a kind of melon in the Cami region. The Portuguese word is melões, not OCR meldes; the source's botanical description is retained without imposing a modern species identification.

runs.text: Adu. Modo de fazer, ou fa-

lines.note: Gives another adverbial form with the caron on ǒ. The gloss begins acting or speaking in an inconspicuous or feigned manner and divides fa-lar.

runs.text: lar dißimuladamente como quem não faz a cou-

lines.note: Explains dissembling as though one were not doing the thing. The scan supports dißimuladamente and não faz, replacing several OCR substitutions and a duplicated vowel.
Completes couſa, then explicitly prefers Sariguenǒ. The cross-reference is a Japanese form embedded in the editorial explanation.
Sarumanako means red eyes compared with a monkey's. The Portuguese noun clearly includes lh, correcting OCR Olos.

runs.text: Os que fazem voltear, ou ſal-

lines.note: Sarumawashi denotes monkey entertainers who make the animals turn or jump. The scan has voltear with t, not OCR volear; ſal- continues below.
Completes saltar os bugios: making the monkeys jump. This finishes the entertainer definition.
Saru nameshi denotes tanned monkey skins. Its italic definition continues on the final row, which the OCR incorrectly grouped with page furniture.

Completes the monkey-skin definition with cured or prepared. The source prints an initial cedilla in çuradas; it is retained as an orthographic anomaly. This body continuation has been separated from the right-hand Saru- catchword while preserving its existing ID.

zones.label: Catchword
zones.note: The former combined bottom-furniture row has been separated: çuradas. is the final body continuation above; Saru- is the independent catchword.
